title: Ion Site Substitution in a Sulfonylcalix[4]arene-Supported Ln8 (Ln = Tb and Eu) Coordination Wheel with Tunable Luminescence

synthesis.procedure: A mixture of H4TC4A-SO2 (0.04 mmol, 34.0 mg), TbCl3·6H2O (0.08 mmol, 30.8 mg), and DL-tartaric acid (0.06 mmol, 6.5 mg) in 3 mL of CH3OH, 6 mL of CHCl3, and 10 μL of DMF was heated at 130 °C for 72 h in a sealed Teflon-lined autoclave and then cooled slowly to room temperature. The solution was gravity-filtered to remove a small amount of insoluble precipitate, and the filtrate was allowed to stand at room temperature. Single crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction appeared after 5–7 days. The crystals were isolated by filtration, washed with cooled CH3OH (3 × 2 mL), and dried in vacuum at 80 °C for 6 h.

properties.summary: Wheel-shaped Tb8 cluster shows strong green Tb(III) luminescence upon ligand excitation. Solid-state QY is 53.3% (lifetime 1.23 ms, λex = 370 nm). In methanol the emission is concentration-dependent, with an optimum near 1.0 × 10−5 mol/L and a best solution QY of 61.8 ± 1.3% (also reported as 61.88%). Characteristic emissions at 492, 547, 586, and 621 nm (5D4 → 7FJ, J = 6–3).

properties.summary: Isostructural Eu8 wheel does not emit under the same ligand-excitation conditions that produce strong Tb8 luminescence. Only negligible emission is observed at λex = 370 or 467 nm, attributed to unmatched TC4A-SO2 → Eu(III) energy transfer and nonradiative decay.

synthesis.procedure: Stepwise synthesis of TbxEu8−x (4 ≤ x < 8): TbCl3·6H2O (0.04 mmol, 15.4 mg) and H4TC4A-SO2 (0.04 mmol, 34.0 mg) (1:1) were mixed in 3 mL of C2H5OH and 6 mL of CHCl3 and refluxed for 0.5 h; then 10 μL of DMF, DL-tartaric acid (0.06 mmol, 6.5 mg), and additional Tb/Eu salts to the overall stoichiometric ratio (Tb:Eu = 15:1, 7:1, 4:1, 6:2, 1:1) were added. Crystalline samples were obtained by the same solvothermal/crystallization process as Ln8. Tb4Eu4 (feed Tb:Eu = 1:1) was fully characterized as the example.

properties.summary: Site-selective Eu doping in the Tb8 wheel gives dual Tb(III)/Eu(III) emission and tunable CIE color until the Tb:Eu ratio approaches 4:4, where effective emission is lost. Solution QY1 of the series falls from 61.88% (Tb8) to 1.22% for Tb4Eu4. Energy transfer is Tb(III) → Eu(III) from 5D4–7F5 (547 nm) and 5D4–7F6 (492 nm) to Eu 5D0; Eu8 and Tb4Eu4 do not exhibit effective emission because bridging Eu interrupts the luminescent pathway.
